Wyandot

Wyandot histories connect the Great Lakes with distinct later communities. The Wyandotte Nation’s account links Detroit, Ohio, Kansas and Oklahoma while explaining important differences within related Wendat histories.

03

Related histories, distinct formations

The Wyandotte Nation explains its formation through survivors of Tionontati, Attignawantan and Wenro communities. Its account distinguishes this later formation from membership in the earlier Huron Confederacy. That distinction helps readers follow related Wendat and Wyandot histories without treating the names as universal synonyms.

Read the sources [4] Wyandotte Nation

04

Following particular community journeys

Lloyd Divine’s account follows settlement near Detroit, later Ohio connections, removal to Kansas and movement to Oklahoma. The page separately names Anderdon in Michigan and the Wyandot Nation of Kansas. These routes invite community-specific reading; the account alone does not determine every group’s present governmental or legal status.

Read the sources [4] Wyandotte Nation

Our History ↗

Publication: Undated; site footer and crawl dates are not publication dates

A Nation-published account with a journey section credited to Lloyd Divine. Distinguishes the later Wyandotte formation from the earlier Huron Confederacy; treaty and termination summaries need originals.

Inspection: Content reviewed for the stated scope

Scope: Actual selected page body read: identification386–389; Detroit/Ohio and other-band statements404–410; Our Journey415–422, credited Lloyd Divine, Wyandotte Nation Cultural Committee; and Are the Wyandotte Huron?428–432. Colonial quotations, sacred symbol explanations, current enrollment counters, event calendar and linked Clarke transcription were excluded. Treaty texts and present recognition determinations for other communities not reviewed.

Review recorded: October 27, 2026
